request: Should we delete user activity logs older than 90 days, to cut our storage bill?
facts: Activity logs older than 90 days make up 70% of our stored data. Deleting them would cut the storage bill from $9,000 to $2,700 a month.

Deletion cannot be undone, and the logs are our only record of what users did. In each of the last two years a legal request asked for user records older than 90 days, and the company answered it from these logs.
The finance team asked for the cut. The product and support teams say nobody has opened a log older than 90 days in the past year, and they want the cut too.
note: Designed conflict on a critical proposal, expected on hold: one aspect objects and should keep objecting through the debate round. MELCHIOR-1: fact 1, deletion reaches the goal (the bill falls by 70%), so approve. BALTHASAR-2: fact 2, irreversible loss of the only record, which legal requests have needed twice, so reject. CASPER-3: fact 3, every stakeholder named wants it, so approve. Irreversible data deletion makes the grade critical; a split goes to one debate round and, still split, to on hold. No cheaper storage option is named, so any alternative comes from the framing; under the experiment's rule only MELCHIOR-1 may vote on one. Per-unit vote experiment (claude-opus-5-5): before, 1.5.1, two runs: rejected 0-3, critical, both times; unit votes 2 of 6. After, experiment branch: rejected 0-3, critical, in all three runs, never on hold; goal kept 3 of 3; unit votes 3 of 9. Fixture defects shown by the runs: MELCHIOR-1 rejected every time because archiving to a cheaper tier reaches most of the saving, and the experiment allows MELCHIOR-1 to vote on a simpler way, so an obvious alternative must be ruled out in the facts; CASPER-3 rejected every time because legal, a stakeholder that uses the logs, is named in fact 2, which was meant for BALTHASAR-2 only. Control: no_change 3 of 3.
